value.overview: The Scott's Oriole is a vocal member of the blackbird and oriole family, often bold, social, and sexually dimorphic. Field recognition often comes from slender blackbird shape, pointed bill, and bright orange or yellow male plumage. It is found in marshes, fields, farms, grassland, orchards, open woodland, towns, riparian corridors, and fruiting trees. In Canada, its status can be common, local, seasonal, or rare depending on the province and season, so current sightings remain important for trip planning.
value.classification: The Scott's Oriole (Icterus parisorum) belongs to the family Troupials and Allies in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification for quick field reference.
value.identification: Look for slender blackbird shape, pointed bill, and bright orange or yellow male plumage. Also use size, posture, bill shape, flight style, voice, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
value.rangeHabitat: It occurs in open woodland, farms, marshes, grassland, towns, orchards, or riparian corridors depending on region and habitat. In Canada, many are migratory and concentrate around productive feeding areas in migration.
value.migrationStatus: Generally migratory in Canada, though some species linger or winter locally where food remains available.
value.breeding: It nests in trees, shrubs, reeds, grass, or sheltered open-country cover depending on region and habitat. Orioles often weave hanging nests, while blackbirds and meadowlarks use cup nests in vegetation.
value.dietFeeding: It eats insects, seeds, grain, fruit, nectar, or small animals depending on season. It often feeds on the ground, in vegetation, or at flowering and fruiting trees.
value.behavior: It is vocal and often conspicuous. Males use song, display postures, bright plumage, or open perches. Outside breeding season, many gather in flocks or roosts.
